subject: Exploring Collaboration Between Our Tay-Sachs Patient Communities
body:
Dear NTSAD team,

My name is Maria, and I lead a patient group for Tay-Sachs disease. I'm writing to introduce our work and explore whether there might be an opportunity to collaborate.

I understand that NTSAD leads work to treat and cure Tay-Sachs, Sandhoff, and GM1 diseases, driving research, forging collaboration, and fostering community [E951b691]. A paper reports that Tay-Sachs disease is caused by a deficiency of the enzyme hexosaminidase-A, resulting in accumulation of GM2 gangliosides [E0d0eb92]. I also understand that NTSAD runs the PRONTO natural history study, which covers GM1 and GM2 conditions including Sandhoff and Tay-Sachs [E48e5738].

Given our shared focus on Tay-Sachs and the related biology across these conditions, I think there could be real value in connecting our communities, whether through sharing resources, coordinating outreach, or simply learning from each other's experience.

Would you be open to a short call, perhaps 20 minutes, to discuss whether a collaboration between our organizations might make sense?

Thank you for considering this. I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Maria
Patient Group Leader

Sources:
[E951b691] https://ntsad.org/about-ntsad/
[E0d0eb92] https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/33232090/
[E48e5738] https://ntsad.org/ntsad-research/research-for-families-and-individuals/natural-history-studies/
